content.text: Move in a way that feels good to you.

meta.name: Three Benefits Promo Post
meta.description: Portrait post with a light wavy-edged side panel on the left holding a logo, a two-line title, a tagline, three icon-led benefit rows and a closing line, a full-body subject cutout over a photo on the right, and a footer bar with an address and a book button; built for promoting a class, service or product through three short benefits.

background.prompt: A full-bleed, photorealistic, eye-level interior or setting that suits the brief's subject (this template: an airy modern pilates studio with a floor-to-ceiling window onto a city skyline, sheer curtains, a few potted plants and a pale stone floor), in portrait format. The left 40–45% of the frame will be covered by a solid side panel with a wavy right edge and the bottom 7% by a footer bar, so put the setting's interest — window, view, depth — in the right half. A floor or ground plane runs across the lower part (about 60–93% down) so the main subject, composited later as a separate cutout, has something to rest on. Soft natural daylight, gentle shadows, calm and uncluttered. Colors and any small accents (plants, props, furniture) follow the brief; add accents only if they genuinely suit its theme, keep them few, subtle and pushed to the far right edge or deep in the background, and never copy this template's own decorations. IMPORTANT: the lower-middle and right of the frame (about 30–100% across, 40–92% down) belongs to a separate transparent subject cutout layer — draw no person, dish, product, equipment, furniture or other subject there, and no people anywhere in the image, not even small or reflected in the distance; keep only the empty floor and wall of the setting continuing naturally behind it, as if the space were cleared for the subject. Even though the brief is about a visual subject, that subject belongs only in the separate cutout layer, never in this background. No text, lettering, logos or watermarks anywhere in the image.
background.notes: No text reads directly on this photo. The logo (Quick Hub black placeholder), the title ('MAKE IT' black, 'YOUR OWN' dark olive rgb(70, 76, 44)), the tagline (black), the three benefit rows (dark olive text beside olive circles with white icons, separated by thin olive rules) and the closing line (bold dark olive) all sit on the solid warm beige side panel rgb(221, 213, 206) on the left, whose wavy right edge is drawn by ellipse layers. The address (white) and the 'Book Your Session' button (olive text on a white button) sit on the olive footer bar layer at the bottom. Panel and footer are layers, not part of this image. Fixed: the clear area for the subject cutout, the floor plane, no people, and the interest kept in the right half. Everything else, including colors, setting and mood, follows the brief.

image.prompt: The main subject the brief is about — a person in action, a product, a dish, a piece of equipment, whichever the request calls for (this template: a woman in olive athletic wear in a prone swan pose on a wooden pilates reformer, seen from the side, facing left). Choose whatever pose, angle and styling naturally suit that kind of subject; for a person this template uses a full-body side view mid-exercise, for an object a three-quarter view resting on the ground. In this portrait frame, place the subject in the lower-middle and right (about 25–100% across, 38–82% down), long and low, facing left toward the copy, filling most of that width; it may run slightly off the right edge. Keep the subject whole and compact with no loose scattered elements near it (sweat, crumbs, splashes, confetti). Soft natural directional light. Subject only, isolated on a fully transparent background: an alpha-channel PNG with no backdrop, floor surface or baked-in shadow. No text, lettering, logos or watermarks anywhere in the image.
image.notes: The hero of the post. The layer is larger than the canvas (it starts left of the panel edge and runs past the right and bottom edges), so the subject must sit only where it shows: right of the side panel, above the footer bar. Its left end tucks just under the panel's wavy edge. It must be a genuine alpha-transparent cutout — only the subject has pixels, never a rectangular backdrop.

slots.notes: Solid olive footer bar carrying the address and the button.

Really the ADDRESS / location: white text in the footer bar next to the map-pin icon, one line. Use only a real location from the request (e.g. '221B Baker Street, London'); otherwise keep the sample. Over ~32 characters it wraps out of the footer bar.
White button panel in the footer, behind the call-to-action and the arrow.

Really the CALL TO ACTION: bold olive text on the white button, followed by the arrow. 2–3 words on one line, e.g. 'Order Online', 'Book a Viewing', 'Shop Now'. The box ends just before the arrow, so anything over ~18 characters wraps out of the button.

image.notes: White map-pin icon at the left of the footer bar, marking the address. Fixed: never regenerate.

slots.notes: White map-pin icon beside the address.
Olive arrow at the right end of the button.

image.notes: Brand logo — reuse the asset exactly as supplied. Never regenerate, recolor, re-crop, or let a filler touch this layer; only ever swap in a different brand's own logo file.

slots.notes: Quick Hub placeholder (logo_black.png, stacked variant) at the top of the beige side panel, above the title.

Really the FIRST TITLE LINE (black serif capitals), read together with the bigger olive line below; ranked subhead only because it is slightly smaller. 1–2 short words that lead into the next line, e.g. 'START' / 'FIND YOUR' / 'TASTE THE'. The panel is narrow, so over ~10 characters it wraps into the second line.

SECOND TITLE LINE, the emphasis word(s): bold olive serif capitals completing the line above, 1–2 short words, e.g. 'FLAVOUR', 'YOUR OWN', 'NEW LOOK'. Very tight: over ~9 characters (e.g. 'DREAM HOME') it wraps or overflows the panel's wavy edge onto the photo.
Tagline under the title, black, one line of 4–6 words, e.g. 'Fresh roasts, every morning.', 'Your new home is waiting.'. Longer copy wraps into the first benefit row.
Olive circle behind benefit 1's icon.
Olive circle behind benefit 2's icon.
Olive circle behind benefit 3's icon.
Thin olive rule under benefit 1.
Thin olive rule under benefit 2.
Thin olive rule under benefit 3.

Benefit 1, first half (regular olive): the lead-in words of a short benefit that continues in the bold line below ('Put on your' + 'favourite music.'). 2–3 words, e.g. 'Pick your' / 'Choose from'. All three benefits share this two-part pattern and should read as parallel phrases. One line only, or it collides with the bold half.
Benefit 1, second half (bold olive): the key words that finish the line above, 1–3 words ending with a period, e.g. 'single origin.', '40+ listings.'. One line only, or it crosses the rule below.
Benefit 2, first half (regular olive), same pattern as benefit 1: 2–3 lead-in words, e.g. 'Roasted fresh' / 'Move in within'. One line only.
Benefit 2, second half (bold olive): 1–3 words ending with a period, e.g. 'every morning.', '30 days.'. One line only, or it crosses the rule below.
Benefit 3, first half (regular olive), same pattern: 2–3 lead-in words, e.g. 'Share it with' / 'Tour it with'. One line only.
Benefit 3, second half (bold olive): 1–3 words ending with a period, e.g. 'the whole family.', 'our agents.'. One line only, or it crosses the rule below.

slots.default_text: Move in a way that feels good to you.
slots.notes: Closing line under the benefits, bold olive, one short sentence over two lines, e.g. 'Coffee the way you like it.', 'Find the home that fits your life.'. Over two lines it runs toward the footer and the subject.
